title: Evening gown: skirt, bodice, and belt, "Venus"
medium: Silk bobbin net with glass seed beads, plastic pearls, plastic sequins, metal sequins, and glass rhinestones in copper alloy settings; silk plain weave; and nylon horsehair
medium_parts: Silk bobbin net with glass seed beads, plastic pearls, plastic sequins, metal sequins, and glass rhinestones in copper alloy settings
identifying_description: Skirt (a)The underskirt consists of a pink silk fabric face, and three layers of stiffened tulle (bobbinet); the pink silk is lined with a single layer of the stiffened bobbinet over the entire area, with an additional double layer of stiffened bobbinet along the lower ⅔ of the skirt. The double bobbinet has been stitched together, so it acts like a single layer. There are no original shaping petticoats or other underpinnings to give the garment volume. There is multi-layer pink silk tulle overskirt, consisting of three layers of fine silk bobbinet (now heavily faded). The edges are raw and unfinished at the hem, and tulle falls in soft folds that are softly gathered into the waistband. There are embellished petals encircling the waist and cascading down the back of the dress in a train. The petals are attached to a double layer of silk tulle that has been stiffened with horsehair braid; this supportive layer is shaped like a peplum at the front of the skirt and morphs into a train at the back. It is constructed in two pieces, the right side and the left side. The two sides of the undertrain are tacked together along their length, leaving an opening to access the zipper at CB. There are 30 overlapping petals adorning the skirt, increasing in size as you descend. Each petal is enforced along its edges with one (or two for the larger petals) strips of synthetic horsehair braid. The petals are highly embellished with sequins in a variety of shapes, sizes, and colors (including large feather-shaped paillettes), as well as faux pearls and rhinestones. . The skirt closes at the CB; 2 hooks and 4 eyes at the waistband (2 set at the end of the waist band, and 2 set further in at a tighter setting and at an angle) an3 hooks/eyes along the opening below the waistband on the petal support (train)Zipper set into silk underskirt It is possible to see that the original color of both the tulle and the faille was a light pink (where both fabrics have been protected at the interior of the CB skirt opening. Bodice (b): The bodice is made from multiple layers of light pink silk tulle, with 7 channels for boning (L front bust, CF, R front bust, R side, R back, CB, L back). There are three main parts of the bodice, as viewed from the exterior: The bodice foundation: contains the corsetry elements, in not embellished, and has a peplum extending below the waist. It consists of 2 layers of tulle, has a sweetheart neckline and dips to mid-back.The waist panel: panel located between the waist and bottom of the bust line. Like a wide belt, this panel consists of 2 layers of tulle, with a pleat running horizontally at the waist. It is embellished with groupings of iridescent circular sequins. The entire bottom edge + top edge along the majority of the front are secured to the bodice foundation; the sides and most of the back edge are not attached to the bodice foundation and contain various fasteners.The bust panels: 2 layers of tulle, each layer is separately and densely embellished with various circular sequins (iridescent and silver colored), as well as large iridescent feather paillettes, clear glass seed beads, and small faux pearls. The bottom edge of the two panels are attached to the bodice foundation, approximately 2 inches below the top edge of the waist panel. The top edges of the two bust panels are scalloped differently, creating an undulating pattern that both hides and reveals the back edge; the two top edges are tacked together at the sides, bust, and CF. At the PR side, the bust panels taper down into the back neckline; on the PL side a triangular piece extends approximately 8" beyond the side of the bodice - this wraps around the back and fastens along the top edge of the bodice at the PR back side. There are three tucks at the PL side and 2 tucks at the PR side bodice foundation (near the underarm); these do not appear original, but they do pre-date the information in the conservation file. CLOSURES: The bodice opens completely along the PL side. There are 15 hooks/eye at the PL edges of the bodice foundationThere are an addition set of 9 hooks/eyes along the PL edges of the waist panel, which fasten over the top of the bodice foundationThe PL triangular extension of the bust panels has a single hook at it's point; this wraps around the back and fastens to a bar located along the top edge at CB, hidden slightly below the waist panel.
web_text: From the debut of his first collection in 1947 until his premature death a decade later, Christian Dior produced garments that served as antidotes to the austere fashions of World War II (1939–1945), with superb construction and tailoring, luxurious fabrics, and sumptuous decorative treatments. The sister gowns Junon and Venus represent the pinnacle of Dior’s creativity. Named after the Roman goddess of marriage and fertility, Junon features glittering sequin embroidery on curved skirt flounces, meant to evoke the feathers of the goddess’s favorite bird, the peacock. With its luminescent, seashell-like skirt flounces, Venus honors the Roman goddess of love, who emerged fully formed from the sea. San Francisco–based luxury department store I. Magnin Company imported these two gowns for in-store presentations along the West Coast, before donating them to the Museums.
